t.3.21.2: This matchless anger of mine, born of the insult done to you, cannot be restrained, like the surging waters of the salt sea.
t.3.21.1: Thus provoked by Śūrpaṇakhā, the valiant Khara then spoke in the midst of the rākṣasas; Khara uttered words harsher still.
t.3.21.4: Let these tears be checked and let this agitation be cast off; I shall lead Rāma together with his brother to the abode of Yama.
t.3.21.3: I do not reckon Rāma, a mere man whose life is already spent, as anything in valour; he, struck down in himself by his own misdeeds, will give up his life-breaths today.
t.3.21.5: Today, O Rākṣasī, you will drink the hot red blood of Rāma, struck down by my axe and lying on the ground with his life ebbing away.
t.3.21.6: Hearing the words that fell from Khara's mouth, she was delighted, and out of folly she again praised her brother, the foremost of the rākṣasas.
t.3.21.7: Harshly reproached by her at first and then praised once again, Khara then spoke to his commander named Dūṣaṇa.
t.3.21.8: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible force, who follow my will and never turn back in battles.
t.3.21.9: Of those terrible ones, dark as blue rain clouds, cruel in their deeds, who delight in harming the world, mighty and of fierce energy.
t.3.21.10: O gentle one, have a full mobilization made of those roused rākṣasas, who have the pride of tigers, huge mouths and great might.
t.3.21.11: Quickly bring me my chariot, gentle one, and my bows, and bright arrows, and swords, and sharp spears of many kinds.
t.3.21.12: Skilled in battle, I wish to march out at the head of the great-souled Paulastyas to slay the insolent Rāma.
t.3.21.13: While he was speaking thus, Dūṣaṇa then announced that the great chariot was ready, bright as the sun and yoked with fine dappled horses.
t.3.21.14: That chariot, shaped like a peak of Meru, adorned with ornaments of refined gold, with golden wheels, spacious, and with a pole made of beryl.
t.3.21.16: In his fury, Khara mounted his chariot, which was furnished with banners and swords, adorned with tinkling bells, and yoked to fine horses.
t.3.21.15: It was adorned all over with golden fishes, flowers, trees, mountains, moons and suns, with auspicious flocks of birds, and with stars.
t.3.21.17: Seeing him mounted on his chariot, the rākṣasas of terrible prowess stood surrounding him and the mighty Dūṣaṇa.
t.3.21.18: Khara, standing in his chariot, looked upon all those rākṣasas, mighty archers bearing fearsome shields, weapons and banners, and said to them, "Set forth!"
t.3.21.19: Then that rākṣasa army, with its dreadful shields, weapons and banners, marched out of Janasthāna with a mighty roar and at great speed.
t.3.21.20: With maces, sharp-edged spears and pikes, with very sharp battle-axes, with swords and discuses held in their hands, and with gleaming lances.
t.3.21.22: Fourteen thousand exceedingly dreadful rākṣasas, obedient to the will of Khara, have marched forth from Janasthāna.
t.3.21.21: With spears and dreadful iron bars, with enormous bows, with maces, swords and pestles, and with thunderbolts gripped in their hands, terrible to behold.
t.3.21.23: But seeing those rākṣasas of fearsome valour rushing forward, Khara's chariot too advanced a little, right after them.
t.3.21.24: Then the charioteer, understanding Khara's intention, urged on those dappled horses adorned with ornaments of refined gold.
t.3.21.25: Urged on swiftly, that chariot of Khara, the slayer of foes, filled the quarters and the intermediate quarters as well with its sound.
t.3.21.26: But Khara, harsh-voiced, his fury swelling, hastening like Antaka to slay his foe, roaring again, urged on his charioteer, mighty as a cloud pouring down a shower of stones.
